title: Capacity Curation: Flexline Slots and Surgical Scope Shearing for Cycle Planning
creator: Priya Kothari
description: Summary: This ticket builds a lightweight, repeatable protocol for allocating limited engineering capacity across concurrent product initiatives for a two-week cycle. The approach (Flexline Slots + Surgical Scope Shearing) aims to preserve delivery predictability while enabling targeted de-scoping that minimizes cross-team churn. Goals: 1) Provide a deterministic, auditable method to allocate role-hours to initiatives (engineer-days, QA-days, infra ops) with a small set of override policies. 2) Define a three-tier scope-trim mechanism (soft de-rate, tactical slice, surgical shear) with clear acceptance criteria and rollback triggers. 3) Produce a one-page playbook and a checklist template for PMs and Eng leads to use during pre-commit and day-5 mid-cycle reviews. Why now: Several initiatives last cycle overran and caused cascading hot-fixes; we need a standardized, low-friction mechanism that teams can adopt without heavy process overhead. Key deliverables: - Flexline slot allocator spreadsheet + autosuggest algorithm (weights: risk, revenue, unblockers, cross-team dependencies) - Scope shearing matrix with examples and canned replacement behaviors - Decision tree for invoking reserve slots, swapping role coverage, and invoking escalation tiers - Playbook doc, a Confluence page, and a short training run for PM/Eng leads
acceptance_criteria: Comparator: run allocator on last three cycles and demonstrate equal-or-better alignment with actual staffing decisions in 80% of scenarios
Playbook published in Confluence with checklist and one example per tier
Two pilot teams adopt the slot allocator for Cycle 46 with at least one de-scope executed using the surgical shear pattern
Post-cycle retrospective template added to measure delivery slippage and collateral work caused by scope cuts
comments: 2026-03-02 - PK: Drafted schematic for Flexline slots. Shared initial spreadsheet with Ash and Marco (links below). Asked Eng leads to validate role-hour assumptions.

2026-03-04 - LO: Reviewed allocator algorithm; added weight for technical debt unblockers and a small penalty for cross-service churn. Raised question about on-call coverage shifts when swapping role ownership.

2026-03-06 - AZ (Engineering): Proposed fallback policy to allocate 20% reserve slots for infra and reliability work; recommended adding an emergency slice that cannot be sheared without Exec approval.
2026-03-08 - PK: Incorporated feedback, updated playbook draft. Reached out to two pilot teams (Search Latency and Console UX) to run a dry allocation this Friday (2026-03-12).
2026-03-11 - LO: Added acceptance criteria for retrospective metrics and a small automation task to export allocator output to CSV. Filed ENG-49210 for automatic export work.
decision_notes: Adopt two complementary knobs: (A) deterministic slot allocator that maps FTE-hours to initiatives by weighted priority; (B) three-tier scope trim (soft de-rate -> tactical slice -> surgical shear). We will treat reliability/infrastructure as first-class reserve with explicit reserve slots. Exceptions require Product Director sign-off. If pilot shows >15% team dissatisfaction or >20% missed deliveries in pilot, rollback to ad-hoc process and iterate.
